method: logical pg_dump sealed with seal.mjs, restored into a clean database
departure: The production drill restores pg_basebackup plus WAL on Linux; this host has no Docker and no Linux cluster, so the drill takes a point-in-time logical dump and restores it into a clean database. The encryption, the clean restore, the API boot, the assertions, and the RTO/RPO reading are the same.

archive.cipher: AES-256-GCM under a random data key wrapped by the key-encryption key
archive.keyCustody: generated for this drill in process memory; never written beside the archive

assertions.name: the restored session has not expired
the lock is in force at the recovery point
the lock has not been lifted
the pending request is pending at the point
the pending request is not verified
the rate-limit window reads as at the point
the health body reports the database
GET /api/v1/auth/session answers 200 with the restored session
the restored session still grants access
the session belongs to the restored account
a guest read stays a guest

rpo.note: The logical dump is the recovery point itself; the state after it is absent. Production bounds the window at 15 minutes with archive_timeout = 60.

acceptanceEstimate.note: The SMS port’s rolling acceptance estimate is process memory (AcceptanceEstimate); a fresh API starts with an empty window and no table holds it.
